messages:
Jada Williams: trying to close on deterministic assignment inputs for route-level A/B. What request fields are actually available at gateway + safe to hash on? also need to handle streaming retries (SSE reconnect) without variant flipping.

Jordan Lee: +1. main thing: we need *entropy* so we don’t accidentally bucket per api key (aka all traffic from a tenant ends up in one variant). If we hash on `api_key_id` that’s basically one bucket per key.

Amara Diallo: at the gateway we can reliably access after auth:
- `tenant_id`, `project_id`, `api_key_id`
- request `path` (route)
- request headers incl `Idempotency-Key` (if client sends)
- we generate `x-redwood-request-id` today (uuid-ish)
We *can* also see IP/user-agent but I’d rather not touch those for privacy + they’re noisy.

Mina Haddad: routing layer has route id + model config (variant A/B) but for assignment we should keep the hash input small + stable. Agree: no IP.

Ravi Menon: streaming retries: current client behavior for `/v1/chat/completions` streaming is they reconnect and resend the request. Some clients include `Idempotency-Key`, some don’t. If they don’t, we currently generate a new request id each time, so any per-request hash will flip variants.

Jada Williams: yep that’s the issue. we saw internal dogfood “variant B traffic higher than configured” and part of it was people retrying streams and getting re-assigned.

Logan Wright: from telemetry POV: please no raw user identifiers or IP in any event. If we do accept a “user key” header from customers, we should treat it as opaque + still HMAC it for bucketing and never emit the raw value in exposure logs.

Jordan Lee: proposal: make stickiness key selection explicit + hierarchical. Something like:
1) if experiment config says `stickiness: header` then use `x-redwood-experiment-key` (customer-provided opaque id)
2) else if `Idempotency-Key` present -> use that (covers retries / stream reconnect)
3) else fallback to `x-redwood-request-id` (per-request random)
Always mix in `tenant_id + experiment_id + route_id` to avoid cross-experiment correlation.

Amara Diallo: gateway can enforce an allowlist of headers we read (`x-redwood-experiment-key`, `Idempotency-Key`). We should *not* start reading random `x-user-id` variants because we’ll regret it.

Mina Haddad: +1. also prefer a Redwood-namespaced header so docs are clear: `x-redwood-experiment-key`.

Ravi Menon: question: if we default to request-id fallback, then the same end-user can get A on one request and B on the next. Is that ok? Or do we require customers to pass experiment-key for user-level stickiness?

Jordan Lee: i think that’s fine for v1. route-level experiments are mostly about aggregate perf/cost/latency. user-level stickiness is “nice” but should be opt-in to avoid privacy issues + absent data.

Ethan Park: agree w Jordan. v1 default can be per-request random assignment (deterministic given request id), and we document “if you want consistent assignment for a user/session, send `x-redwood-experiment-key`”.

Jada Williams: ok but what about stream retry specifically? if they don’t send idempotency key, they’ll flip variants on reconnect and we’ll get weird exposures.

Amara Diallo: can we encourage `Idempotency-Key` in streaming docs + SDKs? We already support it for non-stream to dedupe some client retries.

Ravi Menon: for OpenAI-compatible clients, many already set `Idempotency-Key` (some call it `idempotency_key` but they send header). For the rest, we can update our SDK examples.

Logan Wright: exposure logging should also be careful here: if we see multiple exposures with same `request_id` (?) not possible if request-id changes. If they do send idempotency key, we can treat it as the stickiness key but again: don’t store it raw.

Jordan Lee: +1. Implementation detail:
```
// pseudo
base = `${tenant_id}:${experiment_id}:${route_id}`
key = chooseStickinessKey(headers) // experiment-key > idempotency-key > request-id
bucket = HMAC_SHA256(secret, `${base}:${key}`) % 10000
variant = lookupByTrafficSplit(bucket)
```
This is deterministic, privacy-safe (HMAC), and doesn’t require storing anything.

Mina Haddad: also note: include `route_id` not raw path if possible. paths can include variable segments (e.g. /foo/:id) depending on how we define “route”. For assignment we should use the configured route entity id from control-plane.

Amara Diallo: gateway has the matched route template (we use it for metrics tags today). we can use that as `route_key` until route_id plumbing lands.

Ethan Park: decision check:
- No IP, no UA.
- No `api_key_id` as stickiness key (can still be a *dimension* for access control, but not in the bucket input besides tenant_id).
- Support `x-redwood-experiment-key` (preferred for user/session stickiness; customer-provided opaque).
- Use `Idempotency-Key` when present to stabilize retries/stream reconnect.
- Else fall back to generated request id.

Jada Williams: works for me. any objections?

Logan Wright: only add: we should document “don’t send emails/PII in experiment-key” + we should HMAC with env secret so even if customer sends PII we don’t store it directly. (still: docs + linting in Console would be nice later)

Jordan Lee: :thumbsup: i’ll update the assignment library to take `stickiness_mode` + these header priorities. also will add a unit test for “stream retry with same Idempotency-Key yields same variant”.

Amara Diallo: i can add a gateway log line at debug level showing which stickiness source was used (experiment-key vs idempotency vs request-id), but not the value. helps troubleshooting.

Mina Haddad: please make sure we don’t add that as a metrics tag (cardinality). log only.

Ravi Menon: +1.

Ethan Park: cool. Jada/Jordan can you drop a note in the ADR draft w the header names + precedence? want to lock before we start exposing this in Console.

Jada Williams: will do. thanks all.
